best_for: Windows power users and malware hunters who find Task Manager too shallow and want to see handles, stacks and network connections per process.

points.title: Find what locks a file
points.text: Press Ctrl+F to search handles and DLLs, and you can see which process holds a file you cannot delete or edit. Closing a handle is possible, but the site warns it is a last resort that can corrupt data.

points.title: Deeper than Task Manager
points.text: It shows stack traces with kernel-mode, WOW64 and .NET support, live disk and network activity per process, and GPU graphs for every process. Graph details stay readable even after a process has exited.

points.title: Services and connections
points.text: You can create, edit and control services, and close a process's network connections. Driver services show by default and can be hidden from the View menu.

points.title: Free and MIT licensed
points.text: System Informer is open source under the MIT license, with no paid tier. A portable build runs without installing.

points.title: Windows 10 and later only
points.text: The project lists Windows 10 or higher, 32-bit or 64-bit. There is no macOS or Linux version.

points.title: Listed builds are pre-releases
points.text: The versions here come from the project's si-builds repository, which the team describes as unstable pre-release builds. Stable releases are published in the main GitHub repository. This site keeps 5 Windows versions.
